quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When driving on an interstate:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing. Only stop on the shoulder for emergencies. Change lanes as little as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but you are not in the correct lane, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes then put your vehicle in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the correct lane to turn at an intersection, drive to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance and make turning harder. Tires without enough tread also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when roads are wet.
Keep tires at the correct air pressure.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your vehicle slides on a thin layer of water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure and bad tread increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding also increases the risk.

questions.question: A driver approaching a flashing red traffic light must:
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop. Yield to traffic and pedestrians. Go only when it is safe. At a railroad crossing, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Yield to the train and go only when the lights stop flashing.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:
questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reactions and makes you feel more confident. This causes you to make more driving mistakes.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash through it means that action is not allowed. Right turns are prohibited where this sign is posted.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: A speed that is reasonable and safe for conditions.
A speed safe for existing conditions.

questions.explanation: You must drive at a safe speed for the area, traffic, pedestrians, weather, road condition, and lighting. You must stay within legal speed limits.

questions.question: Driving ability can be impaired by:
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires being in good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs, and drowsiness can all impair driving ability.

questions.question: A steady yellow light at an intersection means:

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Are safe standing on the floor in the back.
Will not get hurt because they are small.
Must never stand in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Use special child seats for small children. No one is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always secure children properly in a seat.

questions.question: Vehicle stopping distance does not depend on:
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition, road condition, and speed. It does not depend on the time of day.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You are in an accident and another person is injured. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: After an accident, do not move the injured person unless you must. Moving them the wrong way can turn minor injuries into serious ones. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, use direct pressure to slow the bleeding.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs mean?
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs tell drivers to let trains go first at railroad crossings. Do not try to drive across the tracks before a train passes.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a line through it mean on a sign?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
Some drivers must yield to other drivers.
You must drive slower than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Some signs tell drivers what they cannot do. These signs are rectangular, white, red, and black. A red circle with a line through a black symbol means that action is not allowed.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so badly they look drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and playing loud music.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so badly they look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they seem drunk. Opening a window, playing music, or drinking coffee does not make a drowsy driver safe on the road.

questions.question: What is most important about speed and curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's weight pushes it to go straight and makes it hard to turn. To stay in control on a curve, you must slow down before you enter it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They get you ready for what is coming. This sign tells you a stop sign is ahead and you need to prepare to stop.

questions.question: When driving, you must stop your vehicle:

options.text: At an intersection with a stop sign.
When a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and when a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
questions.explanation: Crashes often happen when one driver does not see another vehicle or does something unexpected. Talk to other drivers on the road to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Leave more space between your car and the car ahead of you.
Be careful around all other vehicles.

questions.explanation: In snow, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Add more distance between cars because snow makes roads slippery and your car needs more space to stop.

questions.question: Which tip does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Know that tinted windows make it harder to see in the dark.
Keep a flashlight in your car.
Look at the headlights of oncoming cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the headlights of oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: If you look at oncoming headlights, your eyes will shrink. After the car passes, your eyes need time to adjust back to the dark. During this time, you cannot see the road.

questions.question: What does a green arrow with a red light mean?

options.text: You can only drive straight ahead.
You can only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to go in any direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive the way the arrow points, and only if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel hard to force the car back onto the road.
Speed up and steer back onto the road slowly.
Slam on the brakes and stop.
Gently use the brakes to slow down. Turn the steering wheel to get back onto the road safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently use the brakes to slow down. Turn the steering wheel to get back onto the road safely.
questions.explanation: If your car leaves the road, keep the wheels off the pavement and slow down gently with the brakes. When you are going slow enough, turn the steering wheel to get back on the road. Do not turn the wheel hard or fast.
